summary: Describes a format for Message Disposition Notifications and Delivery Status Notifications that carry information about which media features a recipient supports. It lets a sender learn what the receiving system can handle.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines a field that lets a mail or fax recipient report the media features it supports. A sender can use that information to avoid sending a later message the recipient cannot process.

subtitle: A notification field for reporting which media features a mail or fax recipient supports.

tldr.problem: Senders need to know which media features recipients support so that later messages do not exceed their abilities.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a Media-Accept-Features field for Delivery Status Notifications and Message Disposition Notifications.
tldr.outcome: Senders can use the reported feature tags when preparing later messages. Inaccurate information could cause a denial of service.

today: RFC 2530 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Reporting Recipient Capabilities
sections.content:
Internet mail and fax senders need to know what media features a recipient can handle. This RFC defines a format for carrying that information in Delivery Status Notifications (DSNs) and Message Disposition Notifications (MDNs).

DSNs are not available between every sender and receiver. MDNs require the receiver to disclose message disposition information, or, for a denied disposition, the time the notification was generated.
sections.plainLanguage: A recipient can report which media features it supports in a delivery or disposition notification. Senders can use those details when preparing later messages.

sections.title: The Media-Accept-Features Field
sections.content:
The field is named Media-Accept-Features. In a DSN it is a per-recipient field; in an MDN it is an extension field. Its value contains media feature tags, whose meaning is defined in separate schema documents.

Those schema documents must use the media-feature syntax and must be registered according to RFC 2506. The RFC gives an example listing paper size and color, assuming a schema defines those tags.
sections.plainLanguage: The notification adds a field called Media-Accept-Features. Its tags describe capabilities such as paper size or color, when those tags are defined by a registered schema.

sections.title: Message Rejection and Security
sections.content:
If a recipient's mail transfer agent (MTA) determines that it cannot process a message, the RFC strongly encourages it to reject the message with status code 5.6.1. The MTA may return this code when mail data ends if it supports enhanced error codes, or later by sending a delivery failure DSN.

Incorrect feature information could cause later messages to be sent in forms the recipient cannot process. The RFC identifies spoofed DSNs or MDNs and misconfiguration as possible sources of inaccurate information.
sections.plainLanguage: A recipient's mail server is encouraged to reject a message it cannot process. False capability information could lead a sender to send more messages the recipient cannot handle.
